title: Response Tempo Framework and Status Storyboard
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: Describe a tempo-driven approach to incident response (Response Tempo) and provide a reusable status-storyboard template for internal and customer-facing updates. This doc complements the incident command playbook and is intended for SREs, on-call engineers, and incident commanders.

Scope: Applies to production-facing incidents affecting Redwood Inference hosted and dedicated services (API, serving runtime, cache layer, routing). Not intended for purely internal maintenance events unless they impact customer SLA or public status.

Quick summary of the Response Tempo concept

- Response Tempo: a discipline for pacing actions and communications during an incident. It defines discrete rhythms (Beat, Pulse, Cadence) mapped to incident phases to reduce cognitive overload and improve stakeholder alignment.
- Beats are short cycles (1–5 minutes) for immediate triage and mitigation actions.
- Pulses are medium cycles (10–30 minutes) for stabilization and status drafting.
- Cadences are longer intervals (1–4 hours) for leadership updates, customer notices, and retrospection steps.

Ownership and roles

- Document owner: eng-sre team (primary: Asha Patel).
- Typical roles and responsibilities:
  - First Responder: acknowledges alert, collects initial signals, performs quick containment (Beat).
  - Incident Commander (IC): owns timeline, prioritization, and external comms (Pulse/Cadence).
  - Triage Lead: coordinates diagnostics with service owners.
  - Mitigation Squad: executes fixes or rollbacks.
  - Communications Liaison: prepares status page updates and customer templates.
  - Evidence Owner: ensures logs, traces, and artifacts are captured for postmortem.

Incident phases mapped to tempo

1) Detect (Beat) — goal: confirm and scope (0–5 minutes)
   - Accept alert and acknowledge within 1 minute.
   - Quick check: site-wide sensor dashboard, error_rate, latency_p99, request_ingress.
   - If false-positive (spike in telemetry with no customer impact), mark as "monitor" and document in the incident ticket.

2) Triage (Beat → Pulse) — goal: classify severity and impact (5–15 minutes)
   - Determine scope: single-tenant vs multi-tenant, region, specific model or route.
   - Triage checklist:
     1. Confirm customer-facing errors (500s/502s) or SLO breach indicators.
     2. Snapshot recent deploys/rollouts in last 60 minutes.
     3. Identify correlated alerts (storage, network, autoscaler).
   - IC declares severity and opens incident channel.

3) Stabilize (Pulse) — goal: reduce impact and restore partial functionality (15–90 minutes)
   - Apply safe mitigations: traffic routing adjustments, scaling, throttling noisy tenants, model-fallbacks.
   - Use quick rollback or circuit-breaker if suspect deploy.
   - Communications: publish an initial status update (template below) within 30 minutes of incident open.

4) Restore (Pulse → Cadence) — goal: full recovery and validation (90 minutes – several hours)
   - Run validation tests across affected routes and customers.
   - Gradually re-enable functionality and monitor error/latency windows for 30–60 minutes after changes.
   - If restoration is delayed, escalate to executive notification per escalation matrix.

5) Learn (Cadence) — goal: capture evidence, identify root cause, and schedule follow-ups (post-incident)
   - Collect artifacts, tag postmortem owner, and create action items with deadlines.
   - Postmortem draft target: 3 business days, final review and close: 14 days.

Tempo-driven runbook template (use verbatim in incident ticket)

- Incident summary (one sentence):
- Severity: P1 / P2 / P3
- Start timestamp:
- First responder:
- IC:
- Initial scope assessment (services/regions/customers):
- Beat actions completed (list):
- Pulse actions in-progress (list):
- Planned Cadence items (list):
- Next update ETA (minutes):

Containment and mitigation checklist (copy into runbook)

- Safety first: enable traffic mirroring/blackhole for identified bad path.
- If high CPU on GPU nodes: drain and move critical requests to warm pool.
- If KV cache thrashing observed: increase cache TTL for safe prefix sets, enable cache-only routing for critical routes.
- If model quality regression: switch to verified model snapshot variant and pin rollout.
- For unknown failures: reduce ingress via rate-limit override and turn on degraded-mode responses with clear client error codes.

Alert thresholds and SLO trip indicators (examples)

- API error rate > 0.5% for 5 minutes (P2)
- API error rate > 2% for 3 minutes (P1)
- Latency p99 > 4s for 10 minutes (investigate)
- Job queue backpressure > 80% for 15 minutes

Escalation matrix (text table)

Role | Trigger threshold | Contact sequence
------|-------------------|------------------
On-call engineer | Any P1 alert | Pager -> Slack channel -> Call
IC | Unresolved P1 after 20 minutes | IC takes command, notifies eng-sre lead
Eng-sre lead | IC escalation or exec-impact | Call + notify exec ops
Legal/Support (customer-impact) | Data access or regulatory exposure | Notify via secure channel

Status page / customer comms storyboard (use templates below)

Internal status (first 30 minutes) — short form to post in incident channel:
- Title: [INCIDENT] Service latency spike impacting text-generation
- Summary: We are investigating increased latency for the text-generation API in us-west-2. Initial signals indicate a model-serving kernel regression after a recent kernel swap.
- Impact: Intermittent increased latency; some requests timeout.
- ETA for next update: 30 minutes.

Public status page template (customer-facing) — initial post (30 minutes)
- Title: Degraded performance for Redwood API (us-west-2)
- Body: We are experiencing degraded performance for the Redwood API in the us-west-2 region. Our engineers are investigating. Customers may see increased response times or timeouts for text generation requests. We will provide an update within 30 minutes.
- Severity: Partial degradation.
- Customer actions: Retry with exponential backoff. If you have SLA requirements, open a support ticket and reference incident ID: {INCIDENT_ID}.

Public status page template — follow-up (when identified cause)
- Title: Root cause identified — rollback initiated
- Body: We have identified a regression introduced by a kernel selection change in the serving runtime and have initiated a rollback to the previous kernel profile. We expect service restoration within 60 minutes as traffic drains and nodes warm. We will update when we reach full restoration.

Public status page template — resolution
- Title: Service fully restored
- Body: The rollback completed successfully and the Redwood API returned to normal performance at {RESOLVED_AT}. We will publish a post-incident summary within 3 business days.

Status update cadence guidance (IC)

- Initial post: within 30 minutes.
- Regular updates: every 30–60 minutes for P1, every 60–120 minutes for P2 until resolved.
- Resolution post: within 30 minutes of full recovery.

Practical examples and snippets

- Quick status JSON for automated status page API: (fill fields and POST to /status-events)
{
  "incident_id": "INC-2026-XXXX",
  "title": "Degraded performance: Redwood API (us-west-2)",
  "impact": "Partial degradation",
  "started_at": "2026-10-31T14:21:00Z",
  "next_update_eta_minutes": "30"
}

- Slack template for IC to post into incident channel:
/incident update "INC-2026-XXXX" title="Rollback initiated" details="Rollback to kernel v2.14 started; expect recovery in 45–75m; monitoring p99 and error rate"

Game day recipe — 2 hour lab (run quarterly)

Objective: Validate tempo discipline and status-storyboard execution under pressure.
Participants: 1 IC, 2 triage leads, 2 mitigation engineers, 1 comms liaison, 1 observer.
Scenario: Sudden p99 latency spike in us-east-1 after model onboarding.
Schedule:
- 0–5m: Inject alert; first responder acknowledges and performs Beat checklist.
- 5–20m: IC declares severity; comms liaison publishes initial internal status.
- 20–60m: Mitigation squad applies circuit-breaker and rollback; triage lead gathers RCA signals.
- 60–120m: Restore validation, customer status, and create postmortem stub.

Scoring rubric (pass threshold = 80%):
- Acknowledge within 1m (15 pts)
- Initial public status within 30m (20 pts)
- Correct mitigation chosen (25 pts)
- Evidence captured and artifact links posted (20 pts)
- Postmortem stub created before end of lab (20 pts)

Handoff checklist (shift-to-shift)

- Active incidents listed with incident ID and severity.
- Last update timestamp and next update ETA.
- Open mitigation tasks and assigned owners.
- Links to logs, traces, and reproduction steps.
- Contact info for escalation (phone + slack handles).

Retention and evidence policy

- Save key artifacts to incident ticket: dashboards snapshots, flamegraphs, pprof dumps, kernel and model config at time of incident.
- Retain logs and traces for 90 days for P1 incidents and 30 days for non-P1.
- For regulatory-impacting incidents, follow legal evidence procedures and increase retention to 365 days.

Postmortem timeline and quality gates

- Postmortem author assigned within 24 hours.
- Draft posted within 3 business days.
- Peer reviewers: at least 2 (one from eng-sre, one from product/owner).
- All action items must have an owner and a target date.
- Postmortem publish and retro scheduled within 14 days.

Appendix: Common incident play examples (copyable commands)

- Drain GPU node: kubectl cordon node/gpu-023 && kubectl drain node/gpu-023 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
- Pin model variant via API: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/serving/rollouts -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"model_id":"m-bert-quantized-v3","action":"pin"}'
- Post status via CLI helper: redwood-status post --id INC-2026-XXXX --title "Initial update" --body "Investigating increased latency in us-west-2" --visibility public
